text: Nekko Agent is AI help on your computer, for coding and everyday work. It reads, edits, searches and runs things in your projects, using AI that runs on your own machine, an online service you already pay for, or both. It is free, open source and MIT licensed.

heading: Who we are
text: Nekko Agent is made by Nekko Labs. We develop it in the open on GitHub: the code, the plan and the task list are all public. We care about three things: Your computer, your choice. You pick which AI runs, what it can touch and when it needs your approval. Work that uses only local models stays on your machine. Honest software. The app tells you what a model will cost, whether it will fit in memory and what it is about to do. These docs mark what is planned as planned. Fast and calm. The interface never waits on the agent, and responsiveness is measured on every change.

heading: What Nekko Agent does
text: Use AI on your computer or online. Run models with the built in engine, connect Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM, or sign in with a Claude or ChatGPT subscription. Mix them in one workspace. Pick the right AI for each job. Use a capable model for hard work and a small local one for simple tasks. Local models have no per token bill. Work in your real projects. The agent reads, edits and runs code in the folders you add, with diffs to review, guardrails and an optional sandbox. Automate repeat work. heading: Install the app
text: The quickest way to start is the installer. 1. Download the installer for your computer from nekkoagent.com or the latest GitHub release: Windows: the .exe installer macOS (Apple silicon): the .dmg Linux: the .AppImage , or the .deb for Debian and Ubuntu 2. Run it. On macOS, drag Nekko Agent into Applications. 3. Open Nekko Agent, add a project folder and choose a model on the Models tab. macOS builds are signed and notarized, so they open normally. If Windows shows an "unknown publisher" prompt for an unsigned build, choose More info , then Run anyway .

heading: Run it from source
text: Running from source gives you the newest code and is how you work on Nekko Agent itself. It takes four steps: install the prerequisites, clone the repo, install the dependencies, and run npm run dev .

heading: 1. Install the prerequisites
text: You need three tools. Check what you already have:  Git. Any recent version. Get it from git scm.com, or on macOS run xcode select install . Node.js 22.12 or newer , which includes npm. Install the LTS release from nodejs.org, or use a version manager such as nvm or fnm. The project uses npm workspaces, not pnpm or yarn. Rust , through rustup. The engine daemon ( nekkod ) is written in Rust and npm run dev compiles it. You do not need to choose a version: the repo pins one in rust toolchain.toml and rustup installs it on the first build.  On Windows, download and run rustup init.exe from rustu

heading: 4. Start the app
text: This builds the Rust engine daemon and the app, then opens the desktop app. The first run compiles the daemon in release mode and takes several minutes; later runs only rebuild what changed. To stop it, press Enter or q (or Ctrl+C) in the terminal. The app quits normally and stops the engine and any model servers it started.

heading: Other ways to run it
text: Command What it does npm run web The same app in your browser at http://localhost:1440 docker compose up The web edition inside Docker, with your workspaces mounted as volumes npm run build Build everything without launching npm test Run the tests in every workspace

heading: Next steps
text: Take the walkthrough for a tour of the app. Set up local models or sign in with a subscription. Pair your phone to use the agent away from your desk. Want to help build it? Read Contributing and the architecture.

Browsing a provider or opening an existing chat does not change this default; existing chats keep their own model choices. A successfully changed Permissions mode (Ask, Guardrails or YOLO) becomes the default for new chats. Effort applies across chats, and the saved Execution mode is reused through the existing setup flow. Incognito and Offline are different: they apply only to the chat where you enable them and are never

heading: Add windows and read the dock
text: The Agents toolbar provides direct New agent , New image session and New terminal actions, with no ellipsis or overflow button. The empty wall can still open the full window picker. Its Chat, Media and Terminal categories remain horizontal; opening it does not change the wall layout. Each repository heading in the Agent panel also has a plus button for a new agent chat and a terminal button for a new shell in that repository. These actions use the repository you clicked, not another selected or default folder. In Focused view, the new window becomes visible; other layout modes stay unchanged.

heading: Complete, minimize, and delete
text: Hover a window's lifecycle buttons to see the action and hotkey. Shortcuts target the window you are using, not every chat. The X in a chat window's top right corner (and on its card) is Complete : it closes the window and keeps the chat under its group's Show completed control in the left Agent panel for 60 days, where you can read or restore it. Right click a completed chat there for Restore chat or Delete forever without opening it. Completing never deletes; Delete is a separate trash action. Agents you have not touched for a month are completed for you the same way; change or turn this off

heading: A composer that follows your draft
text: In the Command Center, one docked composer targets the selected agent window. Click another agent window to write in that chat's context, or use the dock picker to move the composer above or below the wall. The reply editor grows with new lines and wrapped text, then shrinks when you delete them. In the bottom dock it grows upward, leaving the agent board above it in its own scroll area. Once the draft reaches the height cap, only the editor scrolls; the header, send controls, queued prompts, images and skill rows stay inside the composer ring. A saved manual height remains a preferred minimum

heading: Continue after an interrupted tool
text: After Stop or an interrupted delegation, either type a follow up or use Resume. Both paths repair incomplete tool result history before the next model request. Saved real results are retained; missing results are marked interrupted rather than silently rerunning the tool. A typed follow up stays your own saved message. While a reply is running, queue your follow up or interrupt the current reply; a second direct send is rejected without discarding the queue. Delegation still waits synchronously for the child. Parent callable child status and cancellation while waiting are planned, not availabl

text: Delegation cards start collapsed, including while a child is working or returning a large result. Their compact, plain text activity sentence shares its status with the plan's sub agent list and the working subagent indicator: Working : the child is thinking, writing or using a tool. Waiting : it needs an answer or approval, or is waiting to retry. Completed , Failed or Stopped : recorded terminal events, not guesses based on the presence of a stored reply. Expand a card to read the full task and result in bounded scroll areas. This does not resize the entire agent window. Summaries use existi

heading: Attach photos, videos and any file
text: The + button beside the message box opens a menu with an icon per row: Photo / Video , File , Folder and Skill . Photo / Video follows the model you picked: a model that takes images (Claude, GPT 4o and later, Gemini, Llama vision, LLaVA, Qwen VL and friends) gets the row enabled; a text only model greys it out and the menu says why, so a picture is never attached to a model that cannot see it. Video input is rarer (Gemini, and OpenRouter models that list it); when only photos are accepted the row says photos only . For a local model the app cannot classify, the row stays enabled and the first

heading: Diagrams, tables and code in replies
text: Replies render Markdown: tables, code blocks with a copy button, images, and fenced mermaid diagrams drawn inline. Hover a diagram for Copy (the Mermaid source) and Expand , which opens it in a full window where the mouse wheel zooms, dragging pans, and a double click resets; Escape or Close returns to the chat. The assistant is asked to reach for a diagram when it explains a flow or a structure, a table when it compares, and a code block for anything you might copy.

heading: Plan and capacity at a glance
text: The plan icon in an agent window opens or closes only that chat's plan, sub agents and queue panel. Each chat remembers its own choice locally. Narrow windows fold the panel automatically without changing that choice. The context window gauge has a subtle green background below 60% full, yellow from 60% to below 85%, and red at 85% or higher. Counts remain estimated; an unknown window limit stays neutral. In Agents, the Hardware panel names each detected GPU and shows its own utilization. Missing readings say Unavailable rather than zero; switching monitoring off says Monitor off. VRAM remains

heading: 4. The Context Inspector
text: The right hand panel (toggle it with the panel icon) is Nekko Agent's signature feature. It shows exactly what is entering the prompt this turn , grouped by where it came from: Guidelines : AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules detected in your workspace folders Files : anything you've attached Memory : relevant global / per project notes Connectors : issues, messages, or docs pulled in from Linear/Slack/etc. Each item shows a token estimate , can be toggled off to exclude it, or pinned to always include it. The bar at the top shows how much of the model's context window you're using. No more g

heading: 5. Guardrails & sandbox
text: Open Settings . Two layers keep Nekko Agent from doing something you didn't intend.  Sandbox mode controls how the agent may touch your machine: Mode Behavior Workspace jail (default) File access confined to your added folders; symlinks and junctions that point outside them are refused Ask everything Every write or command requires approval Docker Run shell commands inside a container if Docker is present Off No restrictions (power users) Guardrails classify risky shell commands and decide whether to allow , ask , or deny , per rule, each toggleable. Ships with sensible defaults: recursive for

heading: 6. Projects & the codebase index
text: The Projects tab manages your workspace folders, and yes, multiple roots are supported. Each folder is indexed for files and code symbols (functions, classes, interfaces, types) so the agent and search have a fast map of your code.  Add a folder and it indexes in the background. See file + symbol counts and index status per project. Search across the indexed files instantly, or browse the file list with per file symbol counts.

heading: 7. Memory
text: The Memory tab is a simple, durable knowledge base stored as plain markdown. Keep global memories (preferences, conventions) and per project memories. Relevant entries are surfaced in the Context Inspector and injected automatically, so Nekko Agent remembers how you like to work across sessions.

heading: 8. Connectors
text: The Connectors tab links external sources so their content can be pulled into context: Linear , Slack , Discord (token based), and Gmail / Google Drive (OAuth). Tokens are stored locally. Connect one, fetch a sample to confirm it works, and the results become available to the assistant.

heading: 9. The mascot
text: Nekko Agent is the 8 bit cat that lives at the edge of the window. It waves to say hello, peeks in from the side, and "makes cat biscuits" (kneads its paws) while the model is thinking. Don't want it? Toggle it off in Settings → Appearance.

If Settings or Nekko Server cannot load, the page shows the problem and a Try again button. On desktop, start a stopped service from the tray menu, then retry. In the web edition, check that the Nekko service is running. Existing content stays visible when a refresh fails. Agent shell commands are nonin

Nekko Agent runs models two ways: with its own engine , which needs nothing else installed, or by driving a server you already run (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM). Either way it loads a model with the settings you choose and tells you honestly whether it will fit before you wait through the load. This is what the Models page shows you and why.

heading: The Nekko engine
text: The engine is llama.cpp, managed by Nekko Agent. You press one button, a build comes down from llama.cpp's own releases (about 30 MB for Vulkan or CPU, several hundred MB for CUDA), and the app can serve models. Nothing is downloaded before that press. Which build. Picked from what the GPU probe actually found, not from the platform: CUDA where nvidia smi answers and the card can run it, Vulkan for any other GPU, Metal on Apple Silicon, CPU where there is no evidence of anything else. A slow engine that runs beats a fast one that fails to start. llama.cpp's CUDA build is CUDA 13, which needs a

heading: Reading the fit bar
text: The bar stacks what the model needs against what the device has free: Weights , the model's actual size. Taken from what the server reports or the file on disk, never computed from a parameter count times a quantization width, which is wrong for mixed precision builds like Q4 K M . KV cache , the conversation's memory: 2 x layers x kvHeads x headDim x context x bytesPerElement x parallelSlots . Runtime overhead , compute buffers and the server's own reserve. The marker line is where the device's free memory runs out. Anything drawn past it has to live in system RAM instead.

heading: The verdicts
text: Verdict What it means Fits Everything runs on the GPU with room to spare. Tight It fits, but a long conversation may start spilling. Spills to CPU Part of the model runs on the CPU. It works, several times slower. Will not load It does not fit even using system memory, or the context exceeds the model's own maximum. Unknown The server did not report enough to project it. Unknown is a real answer, not a bug. Nekko Agent will not infer a model's memory use from its name. If the layer count is missing, it says so and names what is missing. A confident wrong number costs you a long load and every

heading: Why a model spills to the CPU
text: Three things push a model off the GPU, in roughly this order of surprise: 1. Context length. The KV cache grows linearly with context. Going from 8k to 64k multiplies it eightfold, and past a point the cache is larger than the model. 2. Parallel slots. Every concurrent slot gets its own full KV cache. Raising OLLAMA NUM PARALLEL from 1 to 4 quadruples the cache at the same context, which is why a model that fit yesterday can stop fitting today with nothing else changed. 3. Something else already resident. The planner measures against free memory, not total, so another loaded model counts again

heading: Apple Silicon
text: A Mac shares one memory pool between the CPU and GPU. The budget is therefore system memory, and Nekko Agent never adds a "VRAM" figure on top of RAM, which would make a 64 GB Mac look like it has 128 GB. The fit drawer says so explicitly when it applies.

heading: Multiple GPUs
text: Two 12 GB cards are not one 24 GB card. Without tensor parallelism a model has to fit on a single device, so the planner measures against the roomiest one and says that it is not pooling them. Only vLLM can split a model across cards, through tensor parallel size .

heading: Settings that need a restart
text: Some settings are read only when the server starts. Ollama's parallelism ( OLLAMA NUM PARALLEL ) and KV cache type ( OLLAMA KV CACHE TYPE ) are both like this. The Advanced section shows them with the exact environment line to set and marks them restart required, rather than offering a control that would quietly not apply. OLLAMA KV CACHE TYPE=q8 0 roughly halves KV cache memory, which is often the cheapest way to fit a longer context.

heading: Stopping a server
text: A server Nekko Agent started is stopped with its own handle, cleanly, and it will not outlive the app. A server that was already running when Nekko Agent found it is somebody else's process: stopping that one asks first and names what it would end, because the thing holding port 11434 might be a service you depend on. LM Studio is the exception that needs no such warning, since it has a real shutdown command rather than a process to kill.

heading: Long tasks on a small context window
text: A local model is often loaded with an 8k or 32k context, and an agent fills that in a few steps: one large file read or one noisy build log is most of it. Nekko Agent keeps the work going rather than stopping when the window fills: It uses the window the model was loaded with , not the model's advertised maximum. LM Studio and the Nekko engine report it in their model list, and Ollama reports it for a loaded model. For anything that reports nothing, it falls back to a guess from the name. Older tool output is left out of the request once the conversation nears 80% of that window. The oldest la

heading: Pictures and models that cannot see
text: Only a vision model with its projector file ( mmproj .gguf ) beside it can look at a picture. The Nekko engine tells the app which of its models have one, so for a text only model such as Qwen3 4B the composer greys out Photo / Video and says why. A picture can still end up in a text only chat: you attached it while a vision model was picked and then switched, or you used a server the app cannot classify. Such a server rejects every request that carries an image, and the image stays in the conversation, so before this guard the chat failed on every later message too. Now, when the model is kno

heading: What is not here yet
text: Browsing and downloading models from inside the app, and a bundled inference engine so a fresh install can run a model with nothing else present, are both planned as separate pieces of work. Today Nekko Agent manages the runtimes you already have.

Nekko Agent can run chat turns on your existing Claude (Pro/Max) or ChatGPT (Plus/Pro/Business) subscription instead of a metered API key. The subscription path is optional: API keys remain available for Anthropic and OpenAI, and local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) still cost $0.

heading: How it works
text: The host side OAuth service runs the sign in flow: 1. Claude We use the same public OAuth client that Claude Code uses. After you click "Sign in with Claude", the app opens a browser to https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize and starts a loopback listener on a local port. After you authorize, Anthropic redirects to the listener with an authorization code. The host exchanges that code for an access token and stores it. 2. ChatGPT / Codex We use the public OAuth client that the Codex CLI uses. The app opens https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize and tries to listen on http://localhost:1455/auth

heading: More than one account
text: You can sign in more than one plan from the same vendor, for example a personal Claude plan and a work one. Each gets its own provider, its own token and its own usage limits. To tell them apart, the app shows the email each one is signed in as next to its name, as in Anthropic (Claude) · you@example.com , in the model picker, the Utilization panel and the Capacity list. The email comes from the sign in itself (Claude's sign in response, or the ChatGPT id token ), stays in tokens.json next to the token, and is not part of a settings export. A plan signed in before this was added shows no email

heading: Caveats
text: Both OAuth clients are the same first party clients used by the vendors' own CLI tools. Anthropic and OpenAI consumer terms are written around their own apps, so using a subscription token with a third party app like Nekko Agent is off label. The flows may stop working at any time if the vendor rotates a client id, changes a scope, or blocks the client. Because of this, the subscription paths are offered as is alongside the API key options, which are unaffected. The features are live validated on the current versions of the vendor flows. If a flow breaks, the fallback paths below still work.

heading: Fallbacks
text: If the browser loopback fails, for example because another process is already using the port, the app falls back to the manual paste path: Claude Copy the code state string the authorization page shows and paste it into the manual code input. ChatGPT If port 1455 is busy, the app switches to manual mode and you copy the code from the page. You can also import a sign in you already did with an official CLI: Claude claude setup token mints a long lived token. Paste that token as the manual code. Codex CLI codex login writes ~/.codex/auth.json . The app can read it and import the same token shape

heading: Security
text: Tokens are stored in tokens.json under the Nekko Agent data directory. The file is created with mode 0600 and the host re applies that permission on startup. tokens.json is never included in a settings export. The export contains only provider configuration (base URL, label, and the opaque tokenKey ), not the access or refresh tokens. The host never sends token values to the renderer. The renderer can only request status, sign out, or re auth through the host. Removing a subscription provider also deletes its stored token from the host.
This page explains where Nekko Agent's usage numbers come from and what they mean.

heading: Where the limit numbers come from
text: The app does not guess your usage. It asks the provider: Claude (Anthropic subscription) Every subscription mode response carries anthropic ratelimit unified headers that report the 5 hour, 7 day, and per model 7 day windows. The host also polls GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage for the first paint and manual refreshes. ChatGPT (Codex subscription) The host polls GET https://chatgpt.com/backend api/wham/usage with the current Bearer token and ChatGPT Account Id . The endpoint returns optional primary window and secondary window usage, plus plan type and credits. These are slots, no

heading: Live reads, not estimates
text: The numbers in the chat header chip and the Models card are live reads from the provider. They update after each subscription response and on a throttled poll. Nekko Agent does not extrapolate or predict your usage locally; if a provider does not return a window, that window is simply not shown.

heading: Utilization and Budget on the Agents wall
text: Utilization deduplicates enabled Claude subscription entries with the same nonempty token key, preferring the Anthropic provider entry. This only changes the displayed account list, not saved providers, credentials or routing. Different accounts/token keys and API key entries stay separate. Budget defaults to 1m . Its ranges use inclusive UTC days: today, 1wk (7 days), 1m (30), 6m (180), 1y (365), and all time through today. The active button has an accent tint and pressed state. All recorded details follow that selection: estimated API spend, input/output tokens, top agent by API cost, local

heading: Off-label caveat
text: The Anthropic and ChatGPT usage endpoints used here are documented by or reverse engineered from the providers' subscription flows. They can change, move, or stop returning data at any time. Nekko Agent is not affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI, and the readouts are provided as a convenience for subscribers, not as an official feature of those services.

heading: Prices are list estimates, not a bill
text: MODEL PRICING in packages/shared/src/limits.ts is a table of published list prices, matched by model id substring. The per model labels ( $X/$Y per MTok ) and the session total in the chat header are estimates only. Your actual provider bill may differ because of taxes, discounts, cached token pricing, batch pricing, enterprise agreements, image or tool token costs, or mid rate changes. Local models (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) and subscription providers are shown as Free or Included in plan because they are not metered through an API key in Nekko Agent.

heading: Limits are provider-side
text: Nekko Agent can only read and surface the limits that Anthropic and OpenAI return. It cannot raise, reset, or bypass them. If a window is reported as rate limited, that state comes from the provider; Nekko Agent does not create or remove the limit.

Drive the Nekko Agent running on your computer from your phone: start and manage chats, watch and steer training runs and goals, approve risky commands, and get a push when a long run finishes. Inference and tools always execute on your machine, under its guardrails; the phone is a thin client.

heading: How it works
text: Your computer dials out to a relay and claims a room. No inbound ports, no port forwarding. Your phone connects to the same relay with the pairing credentials. Every payload is end to end encrypted (AES GCM, key derived from the pairing secret). The relay routes ciphertext; it cannot read prompts, replies, files, or model output. On top of the encrypted transport, every device must pass a handshake against your computer's device registry : new devices enroll only through a single use pairing code that expires in 10 minutes , and your computer answers each device individually (never broadcast).

heading: Pairing a phone
text: 1. On your computer: Settings → Remote access → Enable (the managed relay is prefilled; or paste your self hosted relay URL), then Pair a device . 2. On your phone: scan the QR in the Nekko Agent app ( Computers → Pair a computer ), or with the phone's camera app, which hands the nekko agent pair: link to the Nekko Agent app. Without the app, the pairing link also opens the web app in a browser over the relay, but it is limited to what a phone may do (below), so most desktop screens there are unavailable. 3. The phone shows up under Paired devices , with a live connection dot.

heading: The phone app
text: Native apps. The phone apps are moving to platform native code: Kotlin / Jetpack Compose in apps/android (pairing, chats, live replies, approvals and questions; no phone models yet) and SwiftUI in apps/ios . The Expo app described below stays as the reference until they reach parity. The Android app looks like your desktop by default: Settings → Appearance → Same as computer uses the computer's light or dark theme and its accent color, and follows a change on the computer right away. Pick Phone setting , Light or Dark to choose on the phone instead; that choice is kept on the phone. Only the t

heading: What a paired phone can do
text: Your computer decides what a paired phone may ask for, whatever the phone app does: locking the phone app is not the boundary, your computer is. A phone can use your chats and nothing that changes how the computer itself is set up: Allowed: list, open, start, complete and delete chats; send, queue and stop messages; answer approvals and the agent's questions; pick a model from the computer's providers and a folder from its list; voice status and transcription; and a few settings (below). text: Threat Defense A stranger's PR runs code on your machine None by default this is the big one. Shell steps run unattended, as you, in the workflow's workspace. Only point this at repos you control, or gate it (see below). heading: Limits
text: Local execution only: runs happen on the machine hosting Nekko Agent, with its CPU, its toolchain, and its uptime. A closed laptop is a runner that's down. No parallelism beyond one run per workflow, no job matrix, no artifacts it's a workflow engine, not a CI fleet.

A decision model answers typed questions about a piece of text with calibrated probabilities, in one forward pass, without generating any text. Nekko Agent runs one natively in its engine daemon: Laya , an open weight model from Convai Innovations (Apache 2.0).

heading: What Laya and Jev are
text: TypeSafe Jev is a closed, hosted "System One" decision API: you send a state (text or JSON) and named questions, and get back typed answers. Laya is an open weight model trained for the same job, and its own server ( laya serve ) speaks Jev's request and response shape. Nekko Agent speaks it too, so a Jev client works against the local engine by changing its base URL. Three question types: type criteria answer choice an object of label description, or a list of labels { "type": "choice", "choice": "billing", "confidence": 0.86, "probabilities": { "billing": 0.97, ... } } score the ordered list

heading: The local runtime
text: crates/nekko decide , inside nekkod . No Python at run time: the checkpoint is an ONNX export run by ONNX Runtime (the ort crate with prebuilt binaries), and the tokenizer is the checkpoint's tokenizer.json (the tokenizers crate). Same input as the reference, token for token. Prompt construction, option markers, the 48 token per option cap and the head budget, state truncation (from the back for a conversation list, so the newest turn survives), the Python json.dumps rendering of JSON states and structured criteria, and temperature clamping all follow the laya package (0.3.22). Nekko Agent is one engine and one React UI that run in several places: the desktop app, the self hosted web edition, Docker and the phone. This page is a map of the code for contributors. The full technical plan, with every decision and task, is in TASKS.md ; what the product does and why is in SPEC.md .

heading: The big picture
text: The UI never shares a process with the agent. The window talks to nekkod , the engine daemon, over a loopback connection with a per launch token. The agent loop, terminals and model servers run there, so a busy agent cannot freeze the interface. The engine is moving from TypeScript to Rust. nekkod answers what has been ported natively and passes the rest to the TypeScript host it supervises. Each ported piece has to match the TypeScript behaviour exactly before it takes over. Every edition is the same app. Desktop, web and Docker run the same engine and the same UI. Only the transport differs:

text: Closing the UI already hides it to the tray without stopping the engine. Explicit Quit shuts down the service and managed processes; Stop Nekko service stops the engine without quitting the UI. Neither arrangement promises continued work during OS sleep, shutdown or logout. The 2026 10 13 implementation moves Electron native notifications into main ( apps/desktop/src/main/notifications.ts ), with a direct authenticated engine WebSocket subscription, fresh settings reads per eligible notice, reconnect/backoff and disposal on Quit.
